key_insight: The paper introduces a conservative micro-continuum-cellular automaton framework that couples flow, transport, and biofilm growth while preserving multispecies biomass during interface evolution.
engineering_relevance: It enables more reliable simulation of biofilm dynamics in complex geometries and flows, supporting design and analysis of reactors and other biofouling-prone systems.
method: Couples Darcy-Brinkman-Stokes flow with reactive transport, suspended bacteria, and evolving biofilm as porous media.
Uses a two-stage cellular automaton to redistribute biomass and update biofilm interfaces conservatively.
Accounts for donor/recipient cell volumes to preserve mass and species composition on non-uniform meshes.
evidence_signal: The framework is validated on diffusion-dominated benchmarks, mesh-convergence tests, and a membrane-aerated biofilm reactor case, showing expected morphology and stratification.
watch_item: Accuracy may depend on careful handling of partially occupied cells and mesh non-uniformity, especially when extending to more strongly advective or highly heterogeneous conditions.
paper_title: A conservative micro-continuum-cellular automaton method for multispecies biofilm dynamics in complex flows
